notes: Shopify storefront, direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no blocking. Header mega-menu's top-level 'New & Featured' dropdown lists 'Freshly In Stock' (/collections/freshly-in-stock) alongside seasonal-themed collections (Our Summer Collection, Our Garden Collection, Bathroom Textiles, Summer Accessories). Opened it: real product grid (61 products), rendered count span matches products.json exactly, and its own og:description explicitly frames it as newly-arrived stock: 'We're delighted to report that we have just taken delivery of a flurry of pieces, replenishing our collections and ready to go.' This matches the brief's 'Just In / Just Arrived / Newly Added' target terms and is recorded as the site's New Arrivals PLP. No sub-structure exists for it (single undifferentiated listing; no Furniture/Lighting New-Arrivals children found in the 161-collection taxonomy). Also inspected /collections/available-now (11 products, also in header nav, under the Furniture menu column) per the 'Collection pages need inspection every time' rule -- its title is 'Sofas Available now | Quick Delivery Sofas' and its og:description reads 'Discover our collection of meticulously handcrafted upholstery pieces...available now and ready to be delivered to your doorstep in as little as 7 to 10 days' -- this is a fast-delivery/in-stock-readiness filter on upholstery, not a 'recently added to catalogue' concept, so it was excluded as out of scope (not ambiguous enough to flag; the copy is unambiguous about delivery speed, not newness). The other 'New & Featured' menu items (Our Summer Collection, Our Garden Collection, Bathroom Textiles, Summer Accessories) are seasonal/thematic category collections with no 'new' signal in their names or copy, consistent with the site's normal category taxonomy already covered by the separate Home-Decor/Furniture project -- excluded. Checked main nav, footer nav, sitemap.xml (collections sitemap, 160 entries) and full /collections.json (161 entries); no other New/Just-In/Latest-named collection exists anywhere in the taxonomy.
